brief: Goldman's midday color: the tape turns defensive on fears the Middle East conflict escalates, even as Trump says he won't attack Iran before the midterms, whipsawing price action. WTI holds above $90, yields stay elevated, and SPX outperforms RTY for a 5th session, breaking its 200dma (2,787). AI baskets sell off (Data Centers -370bps, Memory -300bps, Semis -366bps) while defensives (Consumer Staples, Restaurants) and the Most Short basket outperform, and MegaCap vs Non-Profitable Tech dispersion widens. Separately, AVGO is reported in talks to arrange about $30bn in debt financing for OpenAI's custom chip buildout, and Goldman cites a view that real yields stay high because AI compute's 20-30% expected IRRs justify borrowing at high single-digit rates, straining consumers, small businesses, and governments built for cheap capital. Healthcare (XLV) is heavy on one-off names: ARGX's Sjogren's setback, a drug-discovery-basket retrace, and Managed Care STARs jitters. Waller's hawkish shift raises Goldman's conviction in a December 25bp hike. Flow is better-for-sale from both long-onlies and hedge funds across most sectors.
